title: Tom Yum Soup
subtitle: Thai hot and sour prawn soup
excerpt: Tom yum is built on three balancing acts: hot from the chilli, sour from the lime, and salty from the fish sauce. The balance is personal -- taste as you go and adjust each element until it feels right. This version uses ginger and kaffir lime leaves in place of the harder-to-find lemongrass and galangal.
sourceNotes: Tom yum is one of Thailand's most recognised soups, originating in the central Thai plains. The name means boiling (tom) and mixed or blended (yum), referring to the combination of sour, spicy, and fragrant flavours. Lemongrass and galangal are traditional aromatics; ginger and extra lime approximate the flavour profile.

content.text: If your prawns are shell-on, simmer the shells in the stock for 10 minutes first, then strain -- this gives the broth real depth without any extra ingredients. This recipe uses ginger and kaffir lime leaves as accessible substitutes for the traditional lemongrass and galangal.

items.prepNote: sliced into rounds, used as a substitute for galangal
bruised with the back of a knife

content.text: If using shell-on prawns, peel them and simmer the shells in the chicken stock for 10 minutes, then strain and discard the shells. Return the stock to the pan.
Bring the stock to a simmer. Add the kaffir lime leaves, sliced ginger, and bruised chillies. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes. Add the prawns and cook for 2-3 minutes until just pink and curled.

Add the fish sauce, palm sugar, and most of the lime juice. Stir and taste. Adjust the balance with more fish sauce for saltiness, more lime for sourness, or a pinch of extra palm sugar for sweetness.
Add the spring onion and remove from the heat. Serve immediately, scattered with fresh coriander and extra lime on the side.

items.cause: Left in the simmering broth too long.
items.fix: Add the prawns last, cook only until they turn pink, and serve immediately. Residual heat continues to cook them in the bowl.
